claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys can have a fine lamellar microstructure consisting of alternating soft FCC and hard BCC/B2 phases.
The alloy initially has a naturally formed protective surface oxide produced under ambient or lower-temperature conditions.
Mechanical wear at elevated temperature continuously removes or thins the protective oxide film.
Removal of the oxide film exposes interphase boundaries between the soft FCC and hard BCC/B2 lamellae.
Exposed interphase boundaries are electrochemically active and undergo preferential localized corrosion.
Corrosion of the phase interfaces reduces their mechanical integrity.
Corrosion-induced weakening of phase interfaces makes the alloy more susceptible to further wear.
Reciprocal oxide disruption, interfacial corrosion, and interface weakening create a self-reinforcing wear-corrosion cycle.
A protective friction-interface layer can suppress adhesive and oxidative wear at approximately 800°C.
The proposed coupled degradation is expected under simultaneous dynamic mechanical loading and corrosive exposure at approximately 700°C.
Combined wear and corrosion will produce greater total mass loss and surface damage than either isolated wear or isolated corrosion.
The wear rate during combined exposure will be significantly higher than in the matched isolated controls.
Corrosion pit density during combined exposure will be significantly higher than in the matched isolated controls.
An inert environment during wear will maintain the oxide film.
The synergy should be significantly reduced below a critical temperature or when a coating stabilizes the oxide layer.

A controlled comparison should include simultaneous wear-corrosion, wear-only testing in an inert atmosphere, corrosion-only testing without mechanical intervention, and a stabilized-oxide or coated sample.
Failure of oxide stabilization to reduce accelerated degradation, or failure of combined degradation to exceed the sum of isolated wear and corrosion, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says mechanical wear removes or thins the oxide, whereas the baseline assumes that performing wear in an inert environment will maintain the oxide film. Inertness prevents environmental oxidation or corrosion but does not by itself prevent mechanical film removal.

The prediction only requires combined degradation to exceed each isolated response, while the falsification rule requires it to exceed the sum of the isolated responses. A result between the larger individual response and the sum would satisfy the stated prediction but trigger the stated falsification rule.
